biography: Pierre Park, the 'Viking Volcano' as he's becoming known, hails from a small village nestled deep within the Norwegian fjords. Unlike most racers who grew up karting, Pierre's introduction to speed came from navigating icy roads in his beat-up Volvo, a skill honed while delivering groceries for his family's store. His raw talent was undeniable when, at 16, he entered a local ice racing competition, driving a borrowed Lada and astonishingly winning against seasoned veterans. This victory caught the attention of a local sponsor, who helped him enter the national Formula Basic series. While his early results were mixed due to a lack of experience, a podium finish at the notoriously challenging 'Midnight Sun Raceway' proved his potential. Now, at 18, Pierre races as an independent, funded by a patchwork of small sponsors and his family's savings, a stark contrast to the lavishly funded academy drivers he competes against, making his successes all the more impressive.
drivingStyle: Pierre's driving style is as flamboyant as his personality. He's an aggressive late-braker, often pushing the limits of grip to gain positions. While sometimes reckless, his car control is exceptional, allowing him to recover from near-impossible slides. Tire management is still a weakness, often burning through his rubber in the early stages of a race due to his aggressive driving. However, under pressure, Pierre thrives, relishing the chance to make bold moves in high-stakes situations. His raw speed and fearless approach make him a constant threat, but also prone to costly mistakes.

rivalries.reason: Valentina, a product of a prestigious academy, openly criticised Pierre's 'unsportsmanlike' driving after a particularly aggressive overtake at Monza.
Kenji and Pierre clashed repeatedly on track during the Formula Basic season, with several on-track incidents leading to heated exchanges off-track.
Astrid and Pierre are both Scandinavian racers, constantly battling for the title of 'best Scandinavian driver' in the junior categories, creating a fierce but respectful rivalry.

quirks: Always wears a hand-knitted Norwegian sweater under his racing suit.
Listens to black metal music on full volume before every race to 'channel his inner Viking'.
Refuses to drive a car with an odd number as the last digit of its chassis number.
famousQuote: "Smooth is fast, but sometimes you need to be a little rough to remind them you're there!"
careerHighlight: Securing a podium finish at the 'Midnight Sun Raceway' in the Formula Basic series, overcoming mechanical issues and a mid-race spin to finish third.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Norwegian National Ice Racing Championship due to over-aggression, costing him the title.
